_: Footage windows on 29-landlords (defaults, no at= overrides). THE CAMERA MOVES, so each window moves with it: rect / rect_4k are the window at its first visible frame, and track_4k is the footage area for EVERY visible frame, in order from visible_open.in_f to visible_open.out_f − 1 ([x, y, w, h] in 4K px, already rounded; footage frame k goes at track_4k[k], resized to w × h; the aspect stays 16:9). The crane is screen-fixed (moves: false). Rects are the FOOTAGE AREA; the page draws a 2 px cream frame just OUTSIDE each one (4 px at 4K), so footage pasted exactly into the rect sits inside it. Times are seconds from the page's first frame (page 0 = VO 353.96); frames at 30 fps. Render the edit's copy with slots=0 (every window a flat #050507 ground). The four gold windows are lit together and shut together at the same frame; so are the two amber ones. A window that is open longer than its footage holds the footage's last frame (at most 6 frames: Microsoft). Generated by the page itself (29-landlords.html?slotsjson).
wipe: Opening: eased (cubic in-out) over 'opening' (0.28 s): the window first grows as a 2 px horizontal line from its centre out to full width, then opens vertically from its centre line to full height. Closing is the reverse over 'closing' (0.22 s). Simplest composite: paste footage from visible_open.in_f to visible_open.out_f − 1 at track_4k (the window shows its dark ground during the wipes).
composite: for k, (x, y, w, h) in enumerate(slot.track_4k): frame = visible_open.in_f + k; paste footage[min(k, len − 1)] resized to (w, h) at (x, y). The n > len + 6 guard in render-38.py holds here.

overrides: at= on the page query moves every window and the camera keyframes. Open the page with the same at= plus &slotsjson and copy window.SLOTS29_JSON over this file.
present_: Added 3 Oct 2026 (?slotsjson only). slots[].present covers EVERY frame a window is on screen, from its first appearance (the gold quad: frame 0; the amber pair: as its panel fades in; the crane: its opening wipe) until its panel has faded out (or, for the crane, its wipe has shut): frames present.in_f … present.out_f − 1. Per frame k (frame = present.in_f + k): track_4k[k] = the footage area [x, y, w, h] in 4K px (same convention as the old track_4k; it includes the panels' slide-out at the build; frame 0 of a render is drawn before the camera has moved, so its rect is the untransformed world, as the page draws it); state[k] = "dim" (the unlit socket: before the window is named, and again after its lit window has shut) or "lit" (the lit window is drawn: its opening wipe, open, its closing wipe); opacity[k] = the panel's opacity (the dim socket fades with it; 1 for the crane); lit_4k[k] = null when dim, else the part of the footage area the lit window's wipe has opened ([x, y, w, h]; equal to track_4k[k] once fully open), with the 2 px (4 px at 4K) cream frame just outside it. present.lit = the lit frames (in_f … out_f − 1, wipes included) and full_in_f/full_out_f = the fully open frames (= visible_open). The old fields above are unchanged.
